column1: # ZAP DAST rules -- this file is the source of truth for current rule actions.
# Format: rule_id<TAB>action<TAB>description (description is informational only).
# Valid actions: PASS, IGNORE, INFO, WARN, FAIL.
# Rule IDs and matcher behavior can shift between major ZAP versions.
# When upgrading the ``zaproxy/action-api-scan`` action in dast.yml,
# revisit each IGNORE rationale below and confirm the underlying
# behavior has not changed.
# --- Critical: these MUST block the scan when fail_action is enabled ---
# --- Triaged false positives / informational noise ---
# 100001 fires because /docs serves the Scalar UI as HTML and a handful
# of endpoints answer in something other than application/json by
# design: text/event-stream for the SSE streams, the Prometheus text
# format for metrics, text/yaml for a workflow export, and
# application/octet-stream for an artifact download.  That last one is
# the only one with a sniffing dimension and it is already handled:
# the download restricts the type to an allowlist and forces
# Content-Disposition: attachment.  No endpoint anywhere answers
# text/html, so there is no content-sniffing XSS vector for this rule
# to have found.
# 100000 reports 4xx as a class.  A scanner driving every endpoint from
# the OpenAPI schema with literal path parameters and no valid state
# gets validation, auth and not-found refusals by design; that is the
# API working.  A 4xx that IS a defect surfaces as the specific rule
# for it, not as this one.

column3: A Client Error response code was returned by the server

column1: # 10094 reports strings that decode as base64.  Every such value this
# API returns is opaque by construction and goes only to the requester
# who already holds the data: HMAC-signed pagination cursors (a
# tampered one raises rather than decoding), the csrf_token cookie,
# which is a random token the double-submit pattern requires
# JavaScript to read, and the one-time reveal of an API key or a
# WebSocket ticket to the caller that just minted it.  Session and
# refresh JWTs never appear in a response body at all; they travel in
# HttpOnly cookies.
# 90005 reports the absence of Sec-Fetch-* on the REQUEST.  Those are
# headers a browser sets and a scanner does not, so this says something
# about ZAP's own client rather than about the server.  There is no
# server-side behaviour to correct: CSRF is defended by the
# double-submit pattern, and requiring these headers would break every
# non-browser API client.
# 10104 is an active-scan technique, not a finding: it varies the
# User-Agent header to see whether responses change.  Nothing in this
# product branches on User-Agent.
# 90022 / 10023 fire on the substring "Internal Server Error" appearing
# anywhere in a response body.  SynthOrg's RFC 9457 envelope (see
# src/synthorg/core/error_taxonomy.py CATEGORY_TITLES) sets that exact
# title for every ``ErrorCategory.INTERNAL`` response (5xx + 503), so
# the rule matches every legitimate structured 5xx without
# distinguishing it from a real debug-page leak.  Real Python or
# framework debug pages would surface as 500 with framework-specific
# markers, not the curated structured envelope.  Ignore both rules; if a
# regression ever leaks an unstructured stack trace, the underlying
# fact will still surface via test coverage on the exception
# handlers, not via this scanner rule.

column3: Application Error Disclosure (matches RFC 9457 envelope title)
Information Disclosure - Debug Error Messages (same as 90022)

column1: # 10010 fires on the ``csrf_token`` cookie not having ``HttpOnly``.
# That cookie is intentionally non-HttpOnly: SynthOrg uses the
# double-submit-cookie pattern, so the frontend JavaScript MUST be
# able to read the token and echo it back as an ``X-CSRF-Token``
# header.  The actual auth/session cookie IS ``HttpOnly`` (see
# src/synthorg/api/auth/cookies.py).  ZAP's rule has no per-cookie
# scoping, so the only options are global IGNORE or false-positive
# noise on every scan.

column3: Cookie No HttpOnly Flag (csrf_token by design, double-submit)

column1: # 10111 is informational (riskcode=0): ZAP just labels endpoints with
# a ``password`` field as auth requests for its own auth-flow inference.
# Not a finding.
# 10024 is informational (riskcode=0): ZAP flags any URL containing
# the substring "session".  In SynthOrg ``session_id`` is a
# domain/runtime resource identifier (workflow session), NOT an HTTP
# auth token -- auth lives in HttpOnly cookies.  Putting domain IDs
# in query strings is normal REST and does not leak credentials.
# Two URL-borne values this row must not be read as denying, because
# both are deliberate and neither is what the rule reported: the
# WebSocket upgrade accepts a one-time auth ticket as ?ticket= (see
# src/synthorg/api/controllers/ws.py), which is single-use, short-TTL
# and consumed before the socket is accepted, and which the shipped
# dashboard does not use at all (it sends the ticket in the first
# frame instead); and /oauth/callback receives code + state, which is
# the OAuth2 protocol itself.

column3: Sensitive Information in URL (session_id is domain ID)

column1: # 10049 reports a response a cache may store.  Nearly every API
# response here is ``no-store``, pinned by the security-headers
# before_send hook, but the conditional-GET allowlist in
# src/synthorg/api/etag.py deliberately replaces that header on the
# reads it serves ETags for, including authenticated ones
# (/api/v1/settings, /api/v1/security/audit, /api/v1/tasks,
# /api/v1/activities).  Those answer ``private, max-age=0,
# must-revalidate``: a shared cache may not store them at all, and a
# browser must revalidate before every reuse, so what the rule reports
# is a 304 exchange rather than a stored body served without a check.
# The rule cannot distinguish the two.  Plugin 10049 emits several
# alert names depending on the headers it sees, so the same id also
# arrives as "Non-Storable Content", which is pure information; one
# IGNORE covers both.  What still
# catches a regression here is the unit test pinning that exact
# directive string, not this scanner rule; a weaker policy fails the
# suite.

column3: Storable and Cacheable Content (ETag allowlist, revalidated)

column1: # 10062 reports any run of 12 or more digits that starts with a card
# BIN prefix and passes a Luhn check.  Every SynthOrg error response
# carries an RFC 9457 ``instance`` field holding the per-request
# correlation id, a UUID4 minted for each request in
# src/synthorg/api/middleware.py.  A dashed UUID ends in exactly 12 hex
# characters bounded by "-" and a quote, which is the word-boundary
# pair the rule's Maestro arm (5[0678]dd, 6304, 6390 or 67dd followed
# by 8 or more digits) anchors on, so whenever those 12 characters
# happen to be all decimal digits and pass Luhn, the rule reports a
# request id as a card number.  Measured rate: 1.1e-5 per UUID4, about
# one id in 90,000, so a scan of this size trips it roughly once and
# the long run of clean reports before it was not evidence of
# anything.  The reported evidence was 672331071866, and it stands on
# its own: 6723 satisfies the 67dd arm, eight digits follow, the Luhn
# sum is 50, and the string appears nowhere in this repository.  It
# was flagged on POST /setup/complete, which the scan reaches as the
# system role; require_ceo refuses that role, so the body it received
# was the static "Access denied" envelope whose only variable field is
# that correlation id.  The
# High confidence reflects only that ZAP's BIN table holds a record
# for 672331.  The product handles no card, bank account, SSN or
# national-id data anywhere, so this rule has nothing of its kind to
# find, and the suppression cannot be scoped to a URL because every
# entity id in every response has the same shape.
# What this row also covers, and should not be read as denying: an
# operator-authored string can reach a response body (the chosen
# embedder model reference in embedder_failure_reason, an agent,
# provider or model name in the persisted-agent validation message),
# so a name containing a long digit run can be echoed back.  That is
# the operator's own configuration, not stored personal data.
# What still catches a regression: unit tests pin the response shape
# of that endpoint and the field set of the shared error envelope, so
# a numeric field added to either fails the suite instead of passing
# quietly behind this row; and card or SSN patterns in agent tool
# arguments and tool output are matched by the product's own
# fail-closed detector (PII_PATTERNS in
# src/synthorg/security/rules/data_leak_detector.py, plus
# src/synthorg/security/output_scanner.py), a control we own rather
# than a scanner rule.  Introducing any payment or national-id surface
# invalidates this rationale and must revisit it.

column3: PII Disclosure (UUID4 request-id tail matching a card BIN + Luhn)
